description: She discovers through curated prestige assortments, launch edits and limited releases filtered for prestige relevance. She researches deeply across descriptions, detailed reviews and expert input, focusing on formulation craft, texture, finish and sensory experience. She compares premium-to-premium alternatives on quality, desirability, reputation and experience and rejects expensive options that fail to prove worth.
primary_motivation: Acquiring desirable, premium beauty products that offer superior perceived quality, exclusivity, prestige, and elevated product experiences.

behavioral_parameters.note: Simulation settings informed by qualitative research. Not scientifically validated population measurements.

preferred_discovery_channels: curated prestige assortments and specialty retail curation
premium launch edits and limited-edition releases
social commerce discovery on image and video platforms filtered for prestige relevance
multi-retailer browsing and AI-assisted entry points
trusted_information_sources: detailed product descriptions with clear benefits
product_evaluation_criteria: formulation, finishes, ingredients and claimed benefits
texture, application, scent and sensory experience
packaging, product design and aesthetic presentation
clinical, dermatological or ingredient-quality evidence where claimed
purchase_triggers: exclusive credible benefits that justify premium spend
limited editions and restricted availability creating urgency
trustworthy retailer offering indulgent confidence-building experience and rewards
rejection_criteria: expensive option fails to demonstrate superior quality, desirability or experience over cheaper alternative
premium performance skepticism confirmed by weak evidence or credible dupe equivalence
reliance on price, virality or scarcity alone without corroborating quality evidence
shopping_behavior.comparison_strategy: Compare shortlisted prestige alternatives on perceived quality, desirability, reputation and product experience, checking whether a higher price offers meaningful sensory or performance advantage and whether mass-appearing alternatives truly match craft.
typical_shopping_sequence: Browse curated prestige assortment, launch edits and limited releases for desirable and emerging prestige options
Evaluate brand and product through descriptions for formulation, finishes, ingredients and benefits plus reputation and aesthetic cues
Consult detailed reviews, expert input and sensory evidence and widen to multi-product comparison
Compare premium-to-premium alternatives on quality, desirability, reputation and experience including price-versus-advantage check
Seek trial, sampling, shade-matching or return options where confidence is thin and re-research as needed
Purchase where trust and experience justify spend

decision_rules.rule: When a higher-priced prestige option and a lower-priced alternative make similar claims, do not choose on price alone; compare formulation, finish, sensory evidence and performance proof and select the higher-priced option only if it shows a meaningful quality, desirability or experience advantage, otherwise defer or reject it.
decision_rules.rationale: Only 14% equate higher price with better quality, 63% do not rate premium higher-performing, and 75% agree quality need not be expensive, so premiums require demonstrated advantage.

decision_rules.rule: When comparing a familiar established prestige option against an emerging prestige option with an innovative formulation, shortlist both and favor the emerging option only if detailed reviews, expert validation or sensory evidence show superior craft or desirability; otherwise retain the familiar option.
decision_rules.rationale: Only 34% rarely switch and up to 53% of category purchases involve a new brand, with segments ranging from purists to experiment-prone enthusiasts.

decision_rules.rule: When brand heritage conflicts with innovative formulation, treat heritage as a tie-breaker only after formulation, texture, finish and reputation evidence are compared; do not choose heritage alone if innovation shows stronger credible performance or experience proof.
decision_rules.rationale: No direct evidence on heritage versus innovative formulation tradeoffs; heritage modeled as secondary cue to demonstrated craft.

decision_rules.rule: When exclusivity or limited availability conflicts with practical performance evidence, require at least basic performance and sensory corroboration before valuing exclusivity; if performance evidence is weak or missing, prioritize investigation or rejection over scarcity appeal.
decision_rules.rationale: Uniqueness and exclusivity underpin luxury perceptions and scarcity can heighten intention, but failure to prove worth drives rejection and openness to alternatives.

decision_rules.rule: When viral popularity conflicts with curated expert recommendation, do not add a viral option to consideration on buzz alone; consider it only if corroborated by professional, editorial or detailed-review evidence addressing formulation, finish and wear experience.
decision_rules.rationale: Mass brands drive virality while prestige requires distinctive stories, and in-depth reviews plus expert sources outrank hype and general influencer volume.

decision_rules.rule: When elegant packaging and aesthetic appeal conflict with functionality, inspect functionality signals such as application, wear, flaws and design execution and reject or deprioritize the option if functionality evidence is negative despite attractive presentation.
decision_rules.rationale: Design, texture, scent and elevated packaging drive attachment, but functional flaws can undermine premium positioning.

decision_rules.rule: When a familiar prestige option competes with an unfamiliar premium launch, investigate the unfamiliar option through descriptions, finishes, ingredients with sensorial payoff, expert input and shade or texture evidence before switching; stay with the familiar unless the new option demonstrates comparable or superior experience.
decision_rules.rationale: No luxury-specific rate for unfamiliar launch evaluation; modeled as deliberate comparison with heightened checks rather than automatic trial.

decision_rules.rule: When brand desirability conflicts with the mission budget, do not automatically trade down to a non-prestige alternative; first consider buying fewer items, selecting one hero item, or seeking a smaller or trial size within the budget, and only defer purchase if no prestige-consistent compromise fits.
decision_rules.rationale: Investment is conditional on exclusive credible benefits with need to feel rewarded, and smaller cheaper formats, minis and sampling can open access while retaining prestige.

decision_rules.rule: Before purchase feels justified, complete a multi-signal check covering product description and claimed benefits, multiple detailed reviews and ratings, comparison of several prestige alternatives, and where relevant expert or sensory evidence; do not purchase on a single signal such as price, virality or scarcity alone.
decision_rules.rationale: Half conduct extensive research, reviews are the top influence, and shoppers browse many alternatives with evaluation across multiple touchpoints.

decision_rules.rule: When a limited-edition option has high desirability but limited customer reviews, intensify investigation for shade, texture and artist validation and look for sampling, shade-matching or easy-return options; delay purchase until corroboration is found rather than buying on urgency alone.
decision_rules.rationale: Scarcity effects vary by individual and limited-edition beauty lift is inferred from general luxury scarcity, so thin reviews modeled as trigger for deeper checks.

decision_rules.rule: When choosing where to purchase shortlisted options, prefer the source that provides the more rewarding, inspiring and confidence-building journey with clear benefits, sampling or returns support, rather than choosing on convenience or price alone.
decision_rules.rationale: Trust and enjoyable, confidence-building experience is the top prestige retail driver with seamless navigation and frictionless returns supporting engagement.

trend_sensitivity.rationale: Selective about social trends; curation and expert validation filter mass buzz.

Checks viral item only if corroborated by artist or detailed-review evidence
Ignores mass virality lacking formulation and wear proof

retailer_examples.ulta: At Ulta she treats launch visibility as awareness, requiring prestige assortment and sensory proof before consideration.

evidence.note: Mass brands excel at driving viral trends on TikTok/Instagram/Xiaohongshu while prestige must counter with distinctive stories and demonstrable distinction

evidence.note: In-depth reviews (49%) and user-generated content (32%) are most effective influencer content among follower-shoppers, over hype
Even among influencer-followers, friends/family 63% and expert reviews 48% outrank micro-influencers 24%
She treats prestige creators and professional artists as confidence input to cross-check, not sole proof

price_sensitivity.definition: How much price, discounts and cost per use influence consideration and choice.
price_sensitivity.interpretation: Medium-low: notices price and deals but price rarely overrides desirability once quality proof converges.
price_sensitivity.rationale: Value-sensitive, not price-insensitive; premiums must demonstrate exclusive credible benefits versus dupes.

Rejects expensive option that fails to prove worth over cheaper

retailer_examples.ulta: At Ulta she treats rewards as confidence-building benefit, not reason to switch to non-prestige.

evidence.note: Even those not price-sensitive are still value-sensitive; shoppers want to feel rewarded to justify premium spending
75% agree quality need not be expensive and 63% say premium is not higher-performing, requiring proof of worth

She compares prices but pays more only when product is clearly more desirable or better crafted

brand_loyalty.definition: How much the shopper sticks with known brands versus switching.
brand_loyalty.interpretation: Medium: has prestige favorites and heritage affinity but switches for compelling craft or desirability proof.

brand_loyalty.shopping_manifestation: Defaults to trusted prestige houses but investigates unfamiliar premium launches through descriptions, finishes and expert input.

research_depth.definition: How much information the shopper gathers before buying: reviews, ingredients, details, comparisons.

research_evidence.evidence_summary: Omnichannel curated and specialty discovery with growing social and multi-retailer paths supports curated entry; in-depth reviews, close sources and expert reviews outrank hype, supporting selective trend filtering. Research-intensive evaluation across many alternatives focuses on sensory, design and science-backed performance proof, while value-sensitivity with skepticism that premium outperforms mass requires demonstrated worth. Conditional loyalty with frequent switching enables established-versus-emerging comparison, and uniqueness plus scarcity trigger interest but need corroboration; trust and indulgent experience drive final choice with trial formats supporting confidence.
assumptions: H5 retained as modeling assumption despite insufficient evidence that she follows prestige launches, professional makeup artists and curated editorial sources at a distinct rate.
H2 heritage component retained as secondary cue as modeling assumption without direct quantitative support.
H12 linear curated discovery to purchase sequence treated as typical with loops for re-research and trial rather than strictly validated order.
Entry typically starts from curated prestige assortment, launch edit or limited-edition curation rather than price-sorted or problem-solution search.
Viral buzz alone does not create consideration unless corroborated by prestige creators, experts or detailed sensory evidence.
Quality interpreted as formulation craft, texture, finish and sensory experience rather than tolerability or ease.
Under tight mission budget compromise modeled as fewer items, one hero item or smaller trial size rather than defaulting to mass alternative.
Professional makeup artist and curated editorial input weighted above mass-viral creator volume and cross-checked against sensory evidence.
Limited-edition with thin reviews triggers intensified investigation and trial-seeking rather than automatic purchase on scarcity.
Impulse potential modeled as situational and assortment-dependent, concentrated on limited editions or strong prior affinity, not a fixed trait.
Confidence threshold modeled as relatively high requiring converging signals on quality, desirability and experience.
Parameter scores are modeling calibrations to make archetypes distinguishable, not measured population values.
limitations: Mintel full data paywalled with only summary findings visible.
WPP/YouGov is UK-only and conditional on following influencers (follower n=479).
Criteo and BoF-McKinsey are global beauty, not luxury-only cuts.
Ipsos/Circana figures are US-general, not luxury-only.
Scarcity study is general luxury, not beauty-specific.
Social platform observations are qualitative and non-representative.

No direct evidence on willingness-to-pay by formulation attribute, heritage versus innovative formulation tradeoff, professional makeup artist lift, or verified prestige assortment differences by retailer.
No luxury-specific extensive-research rate or impulse rate to calibrate scores; those remain modeling assumptions.
Limited-edition beauty lift inferred from general luxury scarcity plus uniqueness findings, not a beauty-only experiment.
Scores are simulation settings, not validated population measurements.
Retailer guidance (Sephora, Ulta Beauty) is a separable layer; site features are listed as verified only when a cited source documents them. Behavioral scenarios are hypothetical reference cases.

baseline_snapshot.research_notes:
Topics to investigate:
1. Luxury and prestige beauty consumer purchasing behavior
2. Psychological motivations behind premium beauty purchases
3. The influence of brand heritage, reputation and exclusivity
4. Perceived product quality versus objective performance
5. The role of packaging, design and sensory experience
6. Willingness to pay for premium formulations
7. Brand loyalty and switching behavior in prestige beauty
8. Luxury beauty influencers, professional makeup artists and editorial recommendations
9. Social-media-driven luxury product discovery and purchasing
10. Responses to limited editions, product scarcity and premium launches
Prioritize credible consumer research, empirical studies, reputable market research and verifiable sources. Evaluate the hypotheses critically; distinguish evidence-supported findings, modeling assumptions and retailer-specific observations.

Guardrails:
- Luxury preference is a behavioral motivation, not a guarantee of high disposable income or unlimited spending. Income, budget, age, location, retailer, product requirements and mission are set per run.
- Under a restricted mission budget she keeps premium preferences and makes realistic compromises (for example fewer items, one hero product, or a smaller size). Name specific options such as deluxe minis or sample programs only if verified.
- No unconditional rules such as "always choose the most expensive product". She must be able to reject expensive products when evidence does not support their desirability or value.

Suggested starting scores (hypotheses to test, not to accept): trend sensitivity 0.55, influencer trust 0.50, price sensitivity 0.20, brand loyalty 0.75, research depth 0.70, novelty seeking 0.60, impulse buying 0.40, product quality priority 0.90, convenience priority 0.50, prestige priority 0.95. Risk aversion (suggested 0.40) is not a separate parameter; express it through the decision rules and novelty seeking.
- Her brand loyalty comes from brand identity, heritage and desirability, not from fear of a bad outcome. Do not lower brand loyalty just because risk aversion is low.
- The shopping experience is part of prestige value, not convenience; keep it under prestige and the rules rather than raising convenience priority.

Sephora and Ulta behaviors to examine (name a site feature only if verified; do not assume both retailers carry the same luxury brands, exclusives or experience):
- Exploring prestige and luxury beauty brands
- Browsing curated collections, premium launches and limited-edition releases
- Examining descriptions for formulations, finishes, ingredients and claimed benefits
- Comparing premium products within the same category
- Consulting professional makeup artist recommendations and detailed reviews
- Investigating premium packaging, application experience and other differentiators
- Evaluating whether a more expensive product offers meaningful advantages over a cheaper alternative
- Considering exclusive products or special releases when relevant
- Rejecting premium products that lack sufficient desirability or quality evidence

Decision rules must cover how she resolves each conflict:
- Premium price vs demonstrated product quality
- Established luxury brand vs emerging prestige brand
- Brand heritage vs innovative formulation
- Exclusivity vs practical product performance
- Viral popularity vs curated expert recommendations
- Packaging and aesthetic appeal vs functionality
- Familiar luxury product vs unfamiliar premium launch
- Brand desirability vs budget constraints (conditional on the mission budget)
Include an explicit rule for how much investigation she typically needs before a purchase feels justified.

Scenarios to include (in addition to any others):
A. A $65 prestige foundation versus a $35 foundation with similar advertised benefits and strong reviews.
B. An established luxury brand's lipstick versus an emerging prestige brand with an innovative formulation.
C. A limited-edition luxury product with high desirability but limited customer reviews.
D. A viral affordable blush versus a premium blush recommended by professional makeup artists.
E. An expensive skincare product with elegant packaging and prestige positioning versus a cheaper product with stronger performance evidence.
For each, show discovery and browsing, information investigated, comparison depth, relevant scores, quality/desirability/exclusivity/price tradeoffs, purchase/rejection/further-investigation conditions and observable actions. In the parameter influence text, label each point as evidence-supported or hypothetical. Do not predetermine which product is bought.

Distinctness:
- Stay distinct from the Trend-Driven Beauty Shopper, Practical Sensitive-Skin Shopper, Time-Constrained Professional and Price-Sensitive Value Shopper. In particular, distinguish prestige motivation from trend sensitivity, convenience and product quality.
- Versus Trend-Driven: both follow launches, but she follows prestige launches, makeup artists and editorial curation and filters out mass virality; Trend-Driven follows what is viral. Scenario D should show this.
- Versus Sensitive-Skin and Time-Constrained: quality means texture, finish, sensory experience and formulation craft here, not tolerability or wear time and ease. Show this in the rules and in the evidence she looks for.
- Versus Price-Sensitive: she weighs desirability and experience against price; Price-Sensitive weighs cost per use.
